title: Review the spec
why: Five build briefs and a spec that cut across the generator, movement, pre-game, events and the page; the review reads them as the cold build sessions will and checks the claims against the engine's code (step_cost callers, Tile construction sites, End users).

title: Terrain, sizes and the base generator
why: A port of merge4's generator onto hexes with a given recipe; the new judgment (rain shadow, scaling) is small and testable, but it touches Tile, the test helpers (flat() pinned so hand-built tests don't move) and the dev profile's speed, and may move existing tests.

title: Rivers, crossing, floodplains and deltas
why: The new maths: rivers that run to the sea without doubling back, joins, lakes fed and drained, floodplains and deltas, and a crossing cost that changes step_cost's signature under every path the clans walk.

title: Closed country and the open-land guarantee
why: Constructing valleys, sealed valleys and necks on a generated map without breaking the open land, with a retry guarantee and connectivity proofs in the tests.

title: The top-up, events, CLI output and the sweep
why: Well-specified rules and plumbing across steps, then a measured sweep and a bounded tuning pass that reports before and after.

title: The full-screen page
why: Plain JS canvas work with pan, zoom, feed and tooltip, checked by headless Chrome screenshots; many details but no hard algorithms.

title: Review the piece
why: Checks the design bullet by bullet, reruns the sweep, watches the pre-game through the page only, and writes the answer to the piece's question into the PR description.
